Imagine a large scale version of Insurgency with a touch of ARMA...and you've got Squad.

As an early access game, it does lack many features but very enjoyable nonetheless. The atmosphere and intensity of combat is very well done, the crackling sound of bullets and deafening loudness of grenades will make want to hide in a hole and cry. Following orders from your squad leader is a must, it's not an easy game to play, you'll need your squad mates.

Graphic wise it's an upgrade from Insurgency but not quite as nice as ARMA. That said, you wont need an i7 to run the game.

Overall, this online tactical shooter has great potential, and vehicles are coming in July so that should be a great addition.

So immersive! The sounds are just amazing. This is so realistic; you feel like you are actually on a battlefield. The graphics look very cool as well even though it is still in alpha.
This is a different king of fun between an Arma and a COD or Battlefield. Team play is really important and the 50vs50 battles are just breathtaking. It is for a mature audiance and people willing to cooperate. Otherwise, just dont get into this.
Highly recommended.

For almost 300 hours, for a long time, Squad was my 'come-to' for a robust military combat experience. It still is. As an American, I enjoy playing all the Nations. I believe Offworld Industries has facilitated a virtual-space in this way, where we can share perspectives to get a better idea on the realities of warfare, which are difficult, uneasy and exhausting. Squad has connected me to people all over the world and even though we are shooting at one another, or we drop bad nades...flip the trucks, I've felt nothing but connections and compassion rather than diversity and hate. I hope and pray that this game continues to grow and be 'Squad' as we try to settle our Earthly differences. With much love. Tyler K.

Most multiplayer FPS game place you in a group. You lone wolf. You lose interest and move on to the next release.

Squad places you in a team. Success comes from cooperatively working together to achieve a common goal. Everyone must contribute or you risk losing.

This is what gaming is all about. Furthermore, the majority of the community is 18+.

Recent infantry combat overhaul is great. The devs sought to increase the duration of firefights and make cooperation and communication with your teammates essential to winning a firefight. You need a supporting element to suppress an enemy and a moving element to flank. You must work with your squad mates and can no longer lone wolf it. This is where this game truly shines - forcing teamwork among players to be successful. Recent reviewers are upset that they are not as accurate as they once (because they are still trying to nonstop sprint around the map and as a result draining their stamina and making them inaccurate) But the slight reduction in accuracy is an easy to swallow mechanic for the effect of lengthier firefights which are immersive as hell and require you to work with your squad to win.

Before the infantry combat overhaul, you would spend 10 minutes sprinting around the map from one point to the next all for a firefight to end in 2 seconds. And then you would respawn and sprint for another 5-10 minutes to do it all over again. It was not a fun gameplay loop and I started to only fly helicopters to avoid the running simulator + short firefights. Not anymore. The firefights are immersive and fun as hell now. If you are looking for a game which requires you to work very closely with your buddies to win, you will like this game.

Loved this game once, I want to return to it, but the devs keep making poorer and poorer decisions, maybe selling out to tencent is to blame.

They keep making decisions that push away experienced players and bring in new players, this has caused a serious skill issue, where new players dont know what to do and there arent any people to bring them on to coach them up.

And today we find out OWI has spent who knows how long and how much money on porting the game over to console, leaving the existing player base out to dry without new content, or any much needed improvements to gameplay, for a couple thousand more copies on ps5 and xbox?

The best decision in my opinion, is for OWI to revert course back to pre ico, with the few bits of content they added since, and hopefully the old veteran player base will return and build the community back to a healthy state, and after a few more changes and content updates to PC, then an actual serious look at console port could be considered, but imo that is going to fail regardless, only time will tell, good luck!

Players praise the gameplay and the community, while complaints focus on developer updates and bugs and crashes.
